text:
maria: Heads-up — I sketched a proposed Grafana layout + alerting thresholds for compute-accelerator health across regions. Want quick review before I open a PR.

john: sharing a screenshot would help but a short checklist is fine for now. main concerns: ECC spikes, frequent XIDs, and >1% card-flake rate per rack.

maria: agree. rough plan: 1) health score panel (composite) 2) per-region SLOs 3) rolling drain recommendation panel 4) alerting rules + runbook links.

priya: can you define the health score formula? that's the thing folks will argue about. :)

maria: proposed formula (weights): ECC_error_rate * 0.35 + XID_rate * 0.35 + transient_flake_rate * 0.2 + thermal_spike_rate * 0.1. normalize each metric to 0..1 where 1 is worst. health_score = 1 - weighted_sum (so 1 is perfect).

leo: sound reasonable. callouts: weight XIDs higher for older cards; maybe make weight configurable per-hardware-class.

maria: yes — panel will let you pick hardware_class tag to see different weights. default weights above.

sam: SLO suggestion: regional card-availability SLO = 99.95% monthly (counts node-ready / node-total where node=GPU node serving inference). fallback SLO for low-traffic regions = 99.9%.

priya: how do we map "card-availability" to observable signals? is it node-ready + no active ECC/XID alerts for the GPU device?

maria: implementation: availability window = node_ready && (recent ECC_count_per_device < ecc_threshold) && (recent XID_count_per_device < xid_threshold) && (flake_rate_1h < 0.5%). we'll publish thresholds as vars in the dashboard.

john: can you paste the PromQL for the ECC alert? easier to review than prose.

maria: sure — draft alert rule: ```alert: ECCSpikeHigh
expr: increase(nvml_ecc_corrected_total{job="gpu-exporter"}[10m]) / ignoring(instance) group_left() gpu_cards_total > 0 and (increase(nvml_ecc_corrected_total{job="gpu-exporter"}[10m]) > 50)
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: warning
annotations:
  summary: "ECC corrected errors high on {{ $labels.instance }}"
  runbook: "https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-ecc-triage"
```

sam: tweak: use rate over 5m and threshold 10 for newer Ampere, 50 for older. otherwise too noisy. Also add per-card partitioning by device_id.

maria: good catch — will param by hardware_class.

leo: XID rule: consider grouping by driver version and kernel. a pattern of XID+driver combo often points to cuda/driver churn.

maria: runbook checklist (short):
1) check `dmesg` for XID codes and timestamp correlation
2) check `nvml` ECC counters (increase over last 10m)
3) correlate with pod/node GPU utilisation spikes and recent deploys
4) if XID code repeating and ECC_count rising -> mark GPU as candidate for drain
5) run `gpu-memtest` during maintenance window if feasible
6) if passes memtest but flake persists -> schedule replacement (RMA) / escalate to hw team
7) if driver/kernel mismatch -> pin driver or kernel module rollback and monitor

priya: can we add an automated annotation to the dashboard when a drain is initiated? helpful for postmortems.

maria: yes — the drain controller already emits an event we can surface as an annotation. adding it to panel.

monitor-bot: [info] daily summary: region-us-west health_score=0.987, region-eu health_score=0.992, region-apac health_score=0.965. 3 nodes flagged for ECC > region-threshold in us-west.

john: apac looks low — probably the older A100 fleet. cost question: do we want to hide noisy older cards behind dedicated capacity rather than shared pools?

sam: ops note: older cards are cheap capacity but high maintenance. finance wanted a monthly ops cost estimate per flake -> I'll pull last 6 months and post numbers.

leo: visualization request: add small-multiples map showing health_score per-az inside each region (heatmap over map). quick visual makes paging easier.

maria: will add map and an event-filtered timeline (show ECC/XID burst events with links to runbooks). also adding a "proposed action" column that suggests: monitor / schedule-drain / immediate-drain / RMA.

priya: one last thing — SLA impact calc: a card-level outage impacts N tokens/sec. include estimated token-loss if we drain X cards in region to quantify impact on customers.

maria: noted — adding tokens/sec impact and a cost estimate (opportunity cost + replacement ticket estimate).

sam: ok if you open a PR with the dashboard json and a short README linking the runbook and SLO rationale, i'll review and test alerts against the test cluster.

maria: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:

monitor-bot: [deploy] dashboard/create succeeded: dashboards/gpu-health-v2 (sha: d4f2a1).
